svg.title: The derivative films used above are the actual zeroth, first and second coefficient matrices of the local analytic rows. A row’s real directional derivative bound is first converted componentwise, p and then its color-coordinate square sum is taken. For the link row this costs exactly | Loc(G, 1)|; p for the site row it costs | Loc(G, 0)| and the displayed local sampling-density factor. Pulling the site row into the block adds L2, since the normalized site square sum has L4 terms. These are the link and site row allowances used in the weighted operator bounds. The rows are differentiated through third order when constructing a second-order film of their first derivatives; that shift of order is retained.
